title: Feel for Korean
subtitle: Core course · video → learn a whole dialogue by heart → reference sheet

lessons.title: Particles — the bakery (a short story)
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole story by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.en: {On|4} Saturday {I|1} went {to|4} the bakery in my neighborhood.
{At|5} the bakery, {the person at the counter|2} smiled {at|8} me.

sentences.ko: 나{는|1} 크루아상{을|3} 두 개 샀어. 그 사람{도|6} 크루아상{을|3} 좋아한대.
sentences.rd: naneun keuruasangeul du gae sasseo. geu saramdo keuruasangeul joahandae.
sentences.en: {I|1} bought two {croissants|3}. Apparently they love {croissants|3} {too|6}.

sentences.ko: 그날{부터|9} 나{는|1} 매일 아침 빵집{에|4} 가.
sentences.rd: geunalbuteo naneun maeil achim ppangjibe ga.
sentences.en: {Ever since|9} that day, {I|1}'ve been going {to|4} the bakery every morning.

sentences.ko: 일곱 시{부터|9} 여덟 시{까지|9} 빵집{에서|5} 커피{만|7} 마셔.
sentences.rd: ilgop sibuteo yeodeol sikkaji ppangjibeseo keopiman masyeo.
sentences.en: {From|9} seven {to|9} eight, I sit {in|5} the bakery drinking {nothing but|7} coffee.

sentences.ko: 솔직히 빵{보다|10} 그 사람{이|2} 더 좋아.
sentences.rd: soljiki ppangboda geu sarami deo joa.
sentences.en: Honestly, I like {that person|2} more {than|10} the bread.

sentences.ko: 오늘{은|1} 용기{를|3} 내서 쪽지{를|3} 건넸어. "번호 좀 알려 주세요."
sentences.rd: oneureun yonggireul naeseo jjokjireul geonnesseo. "beonho jom allyeo juseyo."
sentences.en: {Today|1} I worked up {the courage|3} and handed over {a note|3}: "Could I get your number?"

sentences.ko: 그 사람{은|1} 웃으면서 쪽지{에|4} 뭔가 적었어.
sentences.rd: geu sarameun useumyeonseo jjokjie mwonga jeogeosseo.
sentences.en: {They|1} smiled and wrote something {on|4} the note.
"I'm married {to|8} the owner. But here's {a coupon|3} instead."

sentences.ko: 그래서 나{는|1} 지금{도|6} 매일 빵집{에|4} 가. 쿠폰{만|7} 계속 쌓여.
sentences.rd: geuraeseo naneun jigeumdo maeil ppangjibe ga. kuponman gyesok ssayeo.
sentences.en: So {I|1} {still|6} go {to|4} the bakery every day. {Only|7} the coupons keep piling up.

footnotes: 은/는 vs 이/가 — 은/는 sets the topic ("as for me…") or contrasts; 이/가 points at who or what. After a consonant 은·이, after a vowel 는·가.
에 vs 에서 — 에 = the place you go to / a point in time (빵집에 가); 에서 = the place where something happens (빵집에서 마셔).
English puts small words in front (to, at, on); Korean glues them to the end of the noun: 빵집에, 빵집에서.
한테 = to/at a person. 하고 = and / with. 부터…까지 = from…to. 보다 = than (it goes after the thing you compare against).
도 (too) and 만 (only) replace 은/는, 이/가, 을/를 — not 그 사람이도, just 그 사람도.

points.head: 은/는  topic · contrast
points.tip: After a consonant 은, after a vowel 는. "As for…". Also contrasts one thing with another.

sentences.en: I'm a student.
I like coffee, but not tea.

points.head: 이/가  subject · new info
points.tip: After a consonant 이, after a vowel 가. Answers to 누가 / 뭐가 always take 이/가. Also with 있다·없다·좋다.

sentences.en: Who came? Yujin did.
I'm hungry.

points.head: 을/를  object
points.tip: After a consonant 을, after a vowel 를. What the action is done to. Often dropped in casual speech.

sentences.en: I'm drinking water.
I'm learning Korean.

points.head: 에 · 에서  to / at · in
points.tip: 에 = destination, time, or where something simply is (있다). 에서 = where an action happens, or "from" a place.

sentences.en: I go to school at three.
I meet my friends at school.

points.head: 도 · 만  too · only
points.tip: Both take the place of 은/는, 이/가, 을/를.

sentences.en: I want to go too.
Today I only drank water.

points.head: 한테 · 하고  to a person · with
points.tip: 한테 = to/at a person (spoken; 에게 in writing, 한테서 = from a person). 하고 = and / with (spoken; 와/과 in writing).

sentences.en: I called my mom.
I watched a movie with a friend.

points.head: 부터 · 까지 · 보다  from · until · than
points.tip: 부터…까지 = from…to (for places 에서…까지 is common). 보다 = than.

sentences.en: I work from nine to six.
Today is colder than yesterday.

lessons.title: Sentence endings — the language exchange
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.en: Hi! I'm studying Korean.
Uh… with someone you've just met, "안녕하세요" is better.
Good day to you! It is an honor to meet you!

sentences.rd: haha, gunin ganneyo. geunyang "bangawoyo" hamyeon dwaeyo.
sentences.en: Haha, you sound like a soldier. Just "반가워요" is fine.
Nice to meet you! Korean is hard, {but|5} it's fun.

sentences.ko: 맞아요. 외국어는 다 어렵{죠|7}. 저도 영어 배우{고|4} 일본어도 배워요.
sentences.rd: majayo. oegugeoneun da eoryeopjyo. jeodo yeongeo baeugo ilboneodo baewoyo.
sentences.en: True. Foreign languages are all hard, {aren't they|7}? I'm learning English, {and|4} Japanese too.

sentences.ko: 그럼 서로 가르쳐 줄{까요|9}? 제가 영어 가르쳐 드릴{게요|8}.
sentences.rd: geureom seoro gareuchyeo julkkayo? jega yeongeo gareuchyeo deurilgeyo.
sentences.en: Then {shall we|9} teach each other? {I'll|8} teach you English.

sentences.ko: 좋아요! 저는 한국어 알려 드릴{게요|8}. 카페 갈{까요|9}?
sentences.rd: joayo! jeoneun hangugeo allyeo deurilgeyo. kape galkkayo?
sentences.en: Deal! And {I'll|8} teach you Korean. {Shall we|9} go to a café?
We're friends now — {should we|9} switch to casual speech?
Sure! …Uh, I mean — affirmative!

sentences.ko: 하하, 군인이 또 왔{네|6}. 괜찮아, 천천히 하{자|3}.
sentences.rd: haha, gunini tto wanne. gwaenchana, cheoncheonhi haja.
sentences.en: Haha, the soldier's back. It's okay, let's take it slow.

sentences.ko: 응! 커피는 내가 살{게|8}. 반말은 어렵{지만|5} 커피는 쉽{지|7}!
sentences.rd: eung! keopineun naega salge. banmareun eoryeopjiman keopineun swipji!
sentences.en: Yeah! {I'll|8} get the coffee. Casual speech is hard, {but|5} coffee's easy, {right|7}?

footnotes: Korean changes the END of the sentence depending on who you're talking to. 해요 (polite, everyday) · 합니다 (formal, announcements) · 해 (casual, close friends only).
Starting with 해 (반말) to a stranger sounds rude; using only 합니다 in a café sounds like a soldier reporting for duty. 해요 is the safe default.
말 놓다 = "to drop the polite endings". Koreans usually ask first: 말 놓을까요? / 말 편하게 해도 돼요?
-네요 = "oh, I see / wow" (you just noticed it). -죠 = "…right?" (you expect agreement). -(으)ㄹ게요 = "I'll (do it for you)". -(으)ㄹ까요 = "shall we / should I?"

points.head: -아요/어요  polite (해요)
points.tip: The everyday polite style for strangers, shops and coworkers. The same form works as a statement or, with rising tone, a question.

sentences.en: I'm going now.
Where are you going?

points.head: -ㅂ니다/습니다  formal (합니다)
points.tip: Announcements, news, speeches, interviews. Questions end in -ㅂ니까/습니까.

sentences.en: Thank you.
We'll be departing shortly.

points.head: -아/어  casual (반말)
points.tip: Drop the 요. Only with close friends, younger people and kids.

sentences.en: I'm hungry.
Where are you right now?

points.head: -고 · -지만  and · but
points.tip: -고 links two actions or facts; -지만 contrasts them.

sentences.en: I eat, then have coffee.
It's pricey, but it's good.

points.head: -네요 · -죠  wow · right?
points.tip: -네요: you've just noticed something. -죠 (-지요): you assume the listener agrees, or you ask softly.

sentences.en: Wow, your Korean is really good!
It's hot today, isn't it?

points.head: -(으)ㄹ게요 · -(으)ㄹ까요  I'll · shall we?
points.tip: -(으)ㄹ게요 = a promise to the listener. -(으)ㄹ까요 = an offer or suggestion.

sentences.en: I'll get in touch.
Should I open the window?

lessons.title: Loanwords — the café
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.rd: aiseu amerikano han janirang chijeukeikeu hana juseyo.
sentences.en: An {iced americano|1} and a slice of {cheesecake|2}, please.
Sure! Do you have a {points card|3}?

sentences.ko: 아니요. 저 여기 처음인데, {와이파이|4} 비밀번호가 뭐예요?
sentences.rd: aniyo. jeo yeogi cheoeuminde, waipai bimilbeonhoga mwoyeyo?
sentences.en: No, it's my first time here. What's the {Wi-Fi|4} password?

sentences.rd: yeongsujeunge isseoyo. noteubuk sseusiryeomyeon jeojjoge konsenteu isseoyo.
sentences.en: It's on the receipt. If you're using a {laptop|5}, there's an {outlet|6} over there.

sentences.ko: 감사합니다. 사실 저 요즘 {아르바이트|7} 찾고 있어요.
sentences.rd: gamsahamnida. sasil jeo yojeum areubaiteu chatgo isseoyo.
sentences.en: Thanks. Actually, I'm looking for a {part-time job|7} these days.

sentences.rd: a, jeodo yeogiseo albahaeyo. keikeuneun seobiseuyeyo.
sentences.en: Oh, I {work part-time|7} here too. The {cake|2} is {on the house|8}.

sentences.ko: 와, 진짜요? 그럼 {셀카|9} 한 장 같이 찍어요!
sentences.rd: wa, jinjjayo? geureom selka han jang gachi jjigeoyo!
sentences.en: Wow, really? Then let's take a {selfie|9} together!

sentences.ko: 좋아요. 근데 제 {핸드폰|10}은 {배터리|3}가 없어서… 손님 걸로 찍어요.
sentences.rd: joayo. geunde je haendeuponeun baeteoriga eopseoseo… sonnim geollo jjigeoyo.
sentences.en: Sure. But my {phone|10} is out of {battery|3}… let's use yours.

sentences.ko: 나중에 유명해지실 것 같으니까 {사인|4}도 해 주세요.
sentences.rd: najunge yumyeonghaejisil geot gateunikka saindo hae juseyo.
sentences.en: You're going to be famous one day, so I'd like your {autograph|4} too.

sentences.ko: 하하, 그럼 영수증 뒤에 해 드릴게요. {알바|7} 찾기 {파이팅|5}!
sentences.rd: haha, geureom yeongsujeung dwie hae deurilgeyo. alba chatgi paiting!
sentences.en: Haha, I'll sign the back of the receipt, then. {Good luck|5} finding a {job|7}!

sentences.ko: 어? "사장님이 {알바|7} 구해요. 내일 면접 보러 오세요!"
sentences.rd: eo? "sajangnimi alba guhaeyo. naeil myeonjeop boreo oseyo!"
sentences.en: Huh? "The owner is hiring a {part-timer|7}. Come in for an interview tomorrow!"

footnotes: Many Korean words are English words in Korean clothes: 와이파이, 배터리, 아메리카노. Say them the Korean way — English pronunciation can actually be harder to understand.
Some are made in Korea: 핸드폰 (hand phone = cell phone), 셀카 (self camera = selfie), 노트북 (notebook = laptop), 원룸 (one room = studio apartment).
False friends: 서비스 = free, on the house · 사인 = autograph or signature · 콘센트 = power outlet · 파이팅 = "you've got this!" (not a fight).
알바 is short for 아르바이트 (from German). 알바하다 = to work a part-time job; 알바생 = a part-timer.

points.head: f · p → ㅍ
points.tip: Korean has no f, so f and p both become ㅍ: fighting → 파이팅, coffee → 커피.

sentences.en: One coffee, please.
What's the Wi-Fi password?

points.head: extra 으
points.tip: Korean syllables can't stack consonants, so 으 is slipped in: cake → 케이크, stress → 스트레스, cream → 크림.

sentences.en: I've been really stressed lately.
Want some ice cream?

points.head: final consonants
points.tip: Only a few sounds can end a syllable: book → 북 (노트북), cup → 컵, chocolate → 초콜릿.

sentences.en: I left my laptop at home.
Do you have paper cups?

points.head: r · l → ㄹ
points.tip: Both become ㄹ. An l in the middle doubles (cola → 콜라); an r at the end usually disappears (computer → 컴퓨터).

sentences.en: Two bottles of cola, please.
My computer froze again.

points.head: v → ㅂ · z, j → ㅈ
points.tip: video → 비디오, service → 서비스, pizza → 피자, juice → 주스.

sentences.en: Shall we order pizza?
Do you have orange juice?

points.head: clipped, made-in-Korea words
points.tip: Korean shortens and remixes: 에어컨 (air conditioner), 리모컨 (remote control), 셀카, 알바, 원룸, 핸드폰.

sentences.en: Could you turn on the AC?
Where's the remote?

points.head: false friends
points.tip: 서비스 = on the house · 사인 = autograph/signature · 콘센트 = outlet · 노트북 = laptop · 파이팅 = you've got this.

sentences.en: This drink is on the house.
Please sign here.

lessons.title: One word, two Korean — the party
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.en: What are {you|1} {wearing|2} to the party today?

sentences.ko: 하하, "{당신|1}"은 부부끼리 쓰는 말이에요. 그냥 "{유진 씨|1}" 해요.
sentences.rd: haha, "dangsin"eun bubukkiri sseuneun marieyo. geunyang "yujin ssi" haeyo.
sentences.en: Haha, "{당신|1}" is what married couples say. Just call me "{Yujin-ssi|1}."

sentences.rd: a, ne. yujin ssineun mwo ibeoyo?
sentences.en: Oh, okay. What are {you|1} {wearing|2}, Yujin?

sentences.rd: wonpiseu ipgo, undonghwa singo, moja sseugo, banji kkil geoyeyo.
sentences.en: I'm {wearing|2} a dress, sneakers, a hat, and a ring.

sentences.ko: 와, 동사가 네 개네요! 파티에 누가 {와요|6}?
sentences.rd: wa, dongsaga ne gaeneyo! patie nuga wayo?
sentences.en: Wow, that's four verbs! Who's {coming|6}?
Some friends and my cousin. Do you {know|3} him?
I {know|3} his name, but we've {never met|3}.

sentences.rd: oppaneun gitareul chyeoyo. urineun bodeugeim hamyeonseo nol geoyeyo.
sentences.en: He {plays|4} guitar. We're going to {play|4} board games and {hang out|4}.

sentences.ko: 저는 피아노 {칠|4} 수 있어요! 거기 피아노 {있어요|5}?
sentences.rd: jeoneun piano chil su isseoyo! geogi piano isseoyo?
sentences.en: I can {play|4} the piano! Do you {have|5} a piano there?

sentences.ko: 피아노는 없는데, 할머니가 {계세요|5}. 노래 진짜 잘하세요.
sentences.rd: pianoneun eomneunde, halmeoniga gyeseyo. norae jinjja jalhaseyo.
sentences.en: No piano — but we do {have|5} my grandma. She's an amazing singer.
Great! I'm {coming|6} right now!

sentences.rd: ppalli wayo! halmeoniga beolsseo maikeu jabeusyeosseoyo.
sentences.en: Hurry, {come|6}! Grandma's already grabbed the mic.

footnotes: you — Koreans rarely say "you". Use the name + 씨, a title (선배님, 팀장님), or nothing. 너 is for close friends; 당신 is for spouses (or arguments).
wear — clothes 입다 · shoes and socks 신다 · hats and glasses 쓰다 · rings and gloves 끼다.
know — 알다 = know a fact or a person. "I've met him" = 만난 적 있어요; "we know each other" = 아는 사이예요.
play — hang out 놀다 · instruments you strike (piano, guitar) and some sports (tennis) 치다 · games and most sports 하다.
come / go — Korean looks from where the SPEAKER is. On the phone "I'm coming!" is 지금 갈게요 (I'm going to where you are).

points.head: you  너 · 당신 · name + 씨
points.tip: Avoid "you". Name + 씨, a title, or drop it. 너 = close friends or younger people only.

sentences.en: Yujin, want some coffee?
What are you doing today?

points.head: wear  입다 · 신다 · 쓰다 · 끼다
points.tip: Korean picks the verb by body part: body 입다, feet 신다, head/face 쓰다, fingers/hands 끼다.

sentences.en: I put on my coat and gloves.
I put on my glasses and sneakers.

points.head: know  알다 · 아는 사이
points.tip: 알다 / 모르다 (not 안 알다). Knowing someone personally: 아는 사람, 아는 사이.

sentences.en: Do you know his number?
We're just acquaintances.

points.head: play  놀다 · 치다 · 하다
points.tip: 놀다 = hang out (no object). 치다 = piano, guitar, tennis. 하다 = games, soccer, most sports.

sentences.en: I hung out with friends over the weekend.
I play the piano and video games too.

points.head: have · be  있다 · 계시다
points.tip: 있다 = there is / I have. An elder's presence → 계시다; an elder's belongings → 있으시다.

sentences.en: Do you have time today?
Grandma is at home right now.

points.head: come · go  오다 · 가다
points.tip: Chosen from the speaker's spot, not the listener's.

sentences.en: I'm coming now!
When are you coming?

lessons.title: Shapes English doesn't have — the picnic
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.en: How many {rolls|3} of gimbap should {we|4} get?

sentences.ko: 세 {줄|3}이요. 그리고 콜라 두 {병|3}, 사과 다섯 {개|3}.
sentences.rd: se juriyo. geurigo kolla du byeong, sagwa daseot gae.
sentences.en: Three {rolls|3}. Plus two {bottles|3} of cola and five apples.

sentences.ko: 사과{는|1} 괜찮아요. {우리|7} 엄마가 벌써 열 {개|3} 싸 주셨{거든요|6}.
sentences.rd: sagwaneun gwaenchanayo. uri eommaga beolsseo yeol gae ssa jusyeotgeodeunyo.
sentences.en: We're good on {apples|1}. {My|7} mom already packed ten, {you see|6}.
Wow, {that's|4} a lot!
But {who|2}'s bringing {the picnic mat|1}?
{I|2} will. {I|4} bought one yesterday.
Oh, {you're|4} all prepared! And {the weather|1}?
Apparently {rain|2}'s coming this afternoon.

sentences.rd: ne? geureom usando du gae sayagenneyo.
sentences.en: What? Then {we|4}'ll need two umbrellas too.

sentences.ko: 아니요, 사실 {우리|7} 집 거실이 넓{거든요|6}. 거기서 피크닉 해요!
sentences.rd: aniyo, sasil uri jip geosiri neolgeodeunyo. geogiseo pikeunik haeyo!
sentences.en: No — actually, {my|7} living room is really big, {you see|6}. Let's have the picnic there!

sentences.ko: 거실 피크닉이요? 좋{네요|5}! 그럼 콜라 한 {병|3} 더!
sentences.rd: geosil pikeunigiyo? jonneyo! geureom kolla han byeong deo!
sentences.en: A living-room picnic? Love it! Then one more {bottle|3} of cola!

footnotes: Topic vs subject — 은/는 changes the subject of conversation ("and the weather?"); 이/가 picks out who or what (누가? → 제가 = "I will, me").
Counters — Korean can't say "two cola"; it needs a counter: 콜라 두 병, 사과 다섯 개, 김밥 세 줄. With counters use 한·두·세·네·다섯.
Dropped subjects — when it's obvious, Korean leaves out I / you / we / it. The words colored only in English have no Korean twin.
-거든요 — gives background the listener didn't know ("…you see"). -네요 — "oh!" as you notice something.
우리 — Koreans say "our" for family and home even when they mean "my": 우리 엄마, 우리 집.

lessons.title: Shapes English doesn't have — at a glance

points.head: 은/는 vs 이/가  topic vs subject
points.tip: 이/가 answers "who / which one?". 은/는 shifts or contrasts the topic.

sentences.en: I'll do it (me, not someone else).
Coffee for me.

points.head: counters  개 · 명 · 잔 · 병 · 장 · 마리
points.tip: Noun + number + counter. Things 개, people 명, cups 잔, bottles 병, flat things 장, animals 마리.

sentences.en: Three students came.

sentences.ko: 물 한 잔이랑 종이 두 장 주세요.
sentences.rd: mul han janirang jongi du jang juseyo.
sentences.en: A glass of water and two sheets of paper, please.

points.head: dropping the subject
points.tip: If it's clear from context, leave out I / you / it.

sentences.en: What did you do yesterday? I saw a movie.
Is it good?

points.head: -네요  oh, I see!
points.tip: Fresh surprise at something you just noticed.

sentences.en: Oh, it's raining outside.
It's already ten, huh.

points.head: -거든요  …you see
points.tip: Gives the background or reason the listener didn't know.

sentences.en: I can't go today. I have an exam, you see.
This place's tteokbokki is famous, you know.

points.head: 우리  "our" = my
points.tip: With family, home, school, company: 우리 엄마, 우리 집, 우리 회사.

sentences.en: My mom's a great cook.
Come over to my place this weekend.

lessons.title: Honorifics — the boss's birthday
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.rd: oneul timjangnim saengsiniraseo jeonyeoge da gachi siksahaeyo.
sentences.en: It's {the team leader|7}'s {birthday|6} today, so we're all having dinner together.
Oh, then should I {get her|2} a cake or something?

sentences.rd: joeunde, timjangnimeun dan geo jal an deuseyo.
sentences.en: Nice thought, but {the boss|7} doesn't really {eat|4} sweets.
Then what does she {like|1}?

sentences.ko: 등산을 좋아하{시고|1}, 주말마다 산에 {계세요|3}. 밤 열 시면 {주무시고요|5}.
sentences.rd: deungsaneul joahasigo, jumalmada sane gyeseyo. bam yeol simyeon jumusigoyo.
sentences.en: She {loves|1} hiking — every weekend she's {out|3} on a mountain. And she's {asleep|5} by ten.

sentences.ko: 민준아, 너 저녁 {먹었어|4}? 선물 고르는 것 좀 도와{줘|2}.
sentences.rd: minjuna, neo jeonyeok meogeosseo? seonmul goreuneun geot jom dowajwo.
sentences.en: Minjun, have you {eaten|4}? {Help me|2} pick out a present.
Yeah, I {ate|4}. Who's it for?

sentences.ko: 우리 팀장님. 등산 좋아하{셔|1}. 등산 양말 어때?
sentences.rd: uri timjangnim. deungsan joahasyeo. deungsan yangmal eottae?
sentences.en: My team leader. She {loves|1} hiking. How about hiking socks?

sentences.rd: gwaenchanne. geunde timjangnim yeonsega eotteoke doesineunde?
sentences.en: Not bad. But how {old|6} {is|1} she?
Happy {birthday|6}, {boss|7}! It's just a little something.

sentences.rd: timjangnim malsseumi, deungsan yangmareun beolsseo seoreun kyeolle isseusidaeyo.
sentences.en: {The boss|7} {says|6} she already {has|3} thirty pairs of hiking socks.

sentences.ko: 아… 그럼 서른한 번째로 받아 주{세요|1}! 오늘은 일찍 {주무세요|5}, {팀장님|7}!
sentences.rd: a… geureom seoreunhan beonjjaero bada juseyo! oneureun iljjik jumuseyo, timjangnim!
sentences.en: Oh… then please take pair number thirty-one! Get some {sleep|5} tonight, {boss|7}!

footnotes: -(으)시- goes inside the verb to raise the person doing it: 좋아해요 → 좋아하세요. Never use it about yourself.
Some verbs have their own honorific word: 먹다 → 드시다, 자다 → 주무시다, 있다 (be somewhere) → 계시다, 말 → 말씀, 생일 → 생신, 나이 → 연세.
주다 → 드리다 when YOU give to someone above you: 사 드릴까요?, 축하드려요.
Notice 민준: he talks to you in 반말, but still raises your boss — 좋아하셔, 되시는데. Honorifics follow the person you talk ABOUT, too.
있으시다 vs 계시다 — the boss HAS socks (있으시다), the boss IS on a mountain (계시다).

points.head: -(으)시-  raising the subject
points.tip: Goes on the verb when the doer is older or higher: 가요 → 가세요, 왔어요 → 오셨어요.

sentences.en: The teacher has arrived.
Where are you headed?

points.head: special verbs  드시다 · 주무시다 · 계시다
points.tip: 먹다·마시다 → 드시다, 자다 → 주무시다, 있다 (be) → 계시다, 말하다 → 말씀하시다.

sentences.en: Grandpa is sleeping right now.
Enjoy your meal.

points.head: 드리다  giving upward
points.tip: 주다 → 드리다 when the receiver is above you. -아/어 드릴게요 = I'll do it for you (politely).

sentences.en: I gave my parents a present.
Let me help you.

points.head: honorific nouns  말씀 · 성함 · 연세 · 생신 · 댁
points.tip: 말 → 말씀, 이름 → 성함, 나이 → 연세, 생일 → 생신, 집 → 댁.

sentences.en: May I have your name?
How old is your grandmother?

points.head: -님 · 께  titles
points.tip: Title + 님: 선생님, 사장님, 팀장님, 고객님. 께 = honorific 한테. Never put 님 on your own title.

sentences.en: Excuse me, could we get the check?
I'll let the team leader know.

points.head: senior vs friend
points.tip: The same question, two ways.

sentences.en: Have you eaten yet? (to a senior)
Did you eat? (to a friend)

lessons.title: Asking & permission — cat-sitting
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.ko: 이번 주말에 우리 고양이 좀 봐 {줄 수 있어요|5}?
sentences.rd: ibeon jumare uri goyangi jom bwa jul su isseoyo?
sentences.en: {Could you|5} look after my cat this weekend?
Of course! {Can I|2} take lots of pictures?

sentences.ko: 네, 많이 찍어 {주세요|1}. 근데 간식은 많이 주{면 안 돼요|3}.
sentences.rd: ne, mani jjigeo juseyo. geunde gansigeun mani jumyeon an dwaeyo.
sentences.en: Yes, {please|1} do! But you {can't|3} give her too many treats.

sentences.ko: 그리고 창문은 열{지 마세요|4}. 자꾸 나가려고 해요.
sentences.rd: geurigo changmuneun yeolji maseyo. jakku nagaryeogo haeyo.
sentences.en: And {don't|4} open the windows. She keeps trying to get out.
Got it. {Is it okay if|2} I sleep on the couch with her?

sentences.ko: 그럼요. 침대에는 올라가{면 안 되는데|3}… 사실 그건 포기했어요.
sentences.rd: geureomyo. chimdaeeneun ollagamyeon an doeneunde… sasil geugeon pogihaesseoyo.
sentences.en: Sure. She's {not allowed|3} on the bed… honestly, I've given up on that one.

sentences.ko: 유진 씨, 고양이가 냉장고 문을 열 {수 있어요|5}?!
sentences.rd: yujin ssi, goyangiga naengjanggo muneul yeol su isseoyo?!
sentences.en: Yujin, {can|5} your cat open the fridge?!
What?! Is it open right now?

sentences.ko: 네… 지금 치즈 먹고 있어요. 뺏{어도 돼요|2}?
sentences.rd: ne… jigeum chijeu meokgo isseoyo. ppaeseodo dwaeyo?
sentences.en: Yeah… she's eating cheese. {Can I|2} take it away from her?

sentences.ko: 빨리 뺏어 {주세요|1}! 그리고 놀라{지 마세요|4}. 원래 그래요.
sentences.rd: ppalli ppaeseo juseyo! geurigo nollaji maseyo. wollae geuraeyo.
sentences.en: Take it, {please|1}, quick! And {don't|4} panic — she always does that.
{Can I|2} tape the fridge shut?
No use. She {can|5} rip tape, too.

footnotes: -아/어 주세요 = "please do it (for me)". 주세요 alone after a noun = "please give me": 물 주세요.
-아/어도 돼요? = "may I / is it okay if…?" Answer: 네, 돼요 / 괜찮아요.
-(으)면 안 돼요 = "you mustn't" (lit. "if you do it, it's not okay"). -지 마세요 = "don't" — a direct request.
-(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 = can (ability or possibility). Asking a favor politely: -아/어 줄 수 있어요?

points.head: -아/어 주세요  please (for me)
points.tip: A polite request. Add 좀 to soften it.

sentences.en: Could you take a picture for me?
Please speak slowly.

points.head: -아/어도 돼요?  may I?
points.tip: Asking permission; without the question it means "it's fine to…".

sentences.en: May I sit here?
It's fine to come tomorrow.

points.head: -(으)면 안 돼요  must not
points.tip: Something is not allowed.

sentences.en: You can't take photos here.
We can't be late.

points.head: -지 마세요  don't
points.tip: A polite "don't". Casual: -지 마.

sentences.en: Don't worry.
Please don't touch.

points.head: -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요?  can you?
points.tip: Ability or possibility. Can't: -(으)ㄹ 수 없어요 or 못 + verb.

sentences.en: Can you read Korean?
Could you give me a hand?

lessons.title: Reasons & experience — tteokbokki
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.ko: 왜 이렇게 늦었어요? 한 시간 기다렸어요.
sentences.rd: wae ireoke neujeosseoyo? han sigan gidaryeosseoyo.
sentences.en: Why are you so late? I waited an hour.

sentences.ko: 미안해요. 버스를 잘못 타{서|1} 종점까지 갔어요.
sentences.rd: mianhaeyo. beoseureul jalmot taseo jongjeomkkaji gasseoyo.
sentences.en: Sorry. I got on the wrong bus, {so|1} I rode it all the way to the last stop.

sentences.ko: 하하, 괜찮아요. 배고프{니까|2} 빨리 뭐 먹으러 가요.
sentences.rd: haha, gwaenchanayo. baegopeunikka ppalli mwo meogeureo gayo.
sentences.en: Haha, it's fine. I'm starving, {so|2} let's go eat something.
Have you {tried|5} tteokbokki?

sentences.ko: 아니요, 아직 먹{은 적 없어요|4}. 매운 맛 {때문에|3} 좀 무서워요.
sentences.rd: aniyo, ajik meogeun jeok eopseoyo. maeun mat ttaemune jom museowoyo.
sentences.en: No, I've {never had|4} it. I'm a little scared {because of|3} the spice.

sentences.ko: 안 매운 것도 있{으니까|2} 한번 먹{어 봐요|5}.
sentences.rd: an maeun geotdo isseunikka hanbeon meogeo bwayo.
sentences.en: There's a mild kind too, {so|2} just {give it a try|5}.

sentences.ko: 와, 너무 맛있{어서|1} 멈출 수가 없어요!
sentences.rd: wa, neomu masisseoseo meomchul suga eopseoyo!
sentences.en: Wow, it's {so|1} good I can't stop!

sentences.ko: 그쵸? 저는 어릴 때 이거 {때문에|3} 요리사가 되고 싶었어요.
sentences.rd: geuchyo? jeoneun eoril ttae igeo ttaemune yorisaga doego sipeosseoyo.
sentences.en: Right? This is {why|3} I wanted to be a chef as a kid.
{Have you ever|4} taken cooking lessons?

sentences.ko: 네, 요리 학원에 한 달 다{녀 봤어요|5}. 근데 불을 두 번 내{서|1} 쫓겨났어요.
sentences.rd: ne, yori hagwone han dal danyeo bwasseoyo. geunde bureul du beon naeseo jjotgyeonasseoyo.
sentences.en: Yeah, I {tried|5} a cooking school for a month. But I started two fires, {so|1} they kicked me out.

sentences.ko: …앞으로도 밖에서 먹어요. 민준 씨 부엌은 위험하{니까|2}.
sentences.rd: …apeurodo bakkeseo meogeoyo. minjun ssi bueokeun wiheomhanikka.
sentences.en: …Let's keep eating out, then. {Since|2} your kitchen is a hazard.

footnotes: -아/어서 and -(으)니까 both mean "so / because". If the second half is a suggestion or order (let's…, please…), use -(으)니까.
Apologies take -아/어서: 늦어서 미안해요 (sorry I'm late). -(으)니까 there sounds like an excuse.
때문에 goes after a noun: 매운 맛 때문에 = because of the spice.
-(으)ㄴ 적 있어요 = "have ever…". -아/어 봤어요 = "have tried / done (it)" — very often used for experience too.

points.head: -아/어서  because / so
points.tip: Natural causes and apologies. Can't be followed by -세요 or -자.

sentences.en: I'm sorry I'm late.
I was tired, so I went to bed early.

points.head: -(으)니까  since (so let's / please)
points.tip: Use when the second half is a suggestion, request or command.

sentences.en: It's raining, so take an umbrella.
We're out of time — let's grab a taxi.

points.head: 때문에  because of
points.tip: After a noun. With verbs: -기 때문에 (a bit formal).

sentences.en: I couldn't go because of a cold.
You made me laugh.

points.head: -(으)ㄴ 적 있어요/없어요  have ever
points.tip: Past experience — or the lack of it.

sentences.en: Have you ever been to Korea?
I've never heard that before.

points.head: -아/어 보다  try
points.tip: "Try doing". In the past tense it means "have done". -아/어 보세요 = give it a try.

sentences.en: Try this.
I've done a bungee jump.

lessons.title: Thoughts & conditions — the night before the interview
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole dialogue by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.ko: 내일 면접인데 잠이 안 와요. 떨어질{까 봐|5} 무서워요.
sentences.rd: naeil myeonjeobinde jami an wayo. tteoreojilkka bwa museowoyo.
sentences.en: My interview's tomorrow and I can't sleep. I'm {scared|5} I'll fail.

sentences.ko: 유진 씨는 잘할 {것 같아요|3}. 준비 많이 했{잖아요|4}.
sentences.rd: yujin ssineun jalhal geot gatayo. junbi mani haetjanayo.
sentences.en: I {think|3} you'll do great. You prepared so much, {you know|4}.
But what {if|1} the interviewers are scary?
{If|1} they're scary, just picture them as puppies.

sentences.rd: haha, geugeo joeun bangbeobin geot gatayo.
sentences.en: Haha, that {sounds like|2} a good trick.

sentences.ko: 그리고 늦잠 잘{까 봐|5} 알람을 다섯 개 맞췄어요.
sentences.rd: geurigo neutjam jalkka bwa allameul daseot gae matchwosseoyo.
sentences.en: And I set five alarms {in case|5} I oversleep.

sentences.ko: 다섯 개{면|1} 옆집 사람도 일어날 {것 같아요|3}.
sentences.rd: daseot gaemyeon yeopjip saramdo ireonal geot gatayo.
sentences.en: {With|1} five, I {think|3} your neighbor will wake up too.

sentences.ko: 괜찮아요. 옆집 사람도 내일 면접이 있{는 것 같아요|2}. 아까 정장 들고 가는 거 봤{잖아요|4}.
sentences.rd: gwaenchanayo. yeopjip saramdo naeil myeonjeobi inneun geot gatayo. akka jeongjang deulgo ganeun geo bwatjanayo.
sentences.en: It's fine. {I think|2} he has an interview tomorrow too. We saw him carrying a suit earlier, {remember|4}?
What {if|1} it's the same company…

sentences.ko: 대박, 진짜 같은 회사였어요! 대기실에서 둘 다 웃음이 터졌어요.
sentences.rd: daebak, jinjja gateun hoesayeosseoyo! daegisireseo dul da useumi teojyeosseoyo.
sentences.en: Unbelievable — it really was the same company! We both burst out laughing in the waiting room.
So did you both get in?

sentences.ko: 결과는 아직 몰라요. 근데 저녁 먹자고 하는 거 보면… 뭔가 붙은 {것 같아요|2}.
sentences.rd: gyeolgwaneun ajik mollayo. geunde jeonyeok meokjago haneun geo bomyeon… mwonga buteun geot gatayo.
sentences.en: No results yet. But he asked me to dinner, so… {I think|2} I passed something.

footnotes: -(으)면 = if / when. It can also mean "with / at" after a number: 다섯 개면 = with five.
-는 것 같아요 = it seems (from what I see now) — also used just to sound softer. -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요 = I think it will. -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 = I think it did.
-잖아요 = "you know / remember?" — reminds the listener of something you both know. With a stranger it can sound pushy.
-(으)ㄹ까 봐 = "in case / for fear that": 늦잠 잘까 봐 = in case I oversleep.

points.head: -(으)면  if / when
points.tip: Conditions and "whenever".

sentences.en: If you have time, let's go together.
When spring comes, the flowers bloom.

points.head: -는 것 같아요  it seems
points.tip: A soft guess from what you see now. Past: -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요. Noun: -인 것 같아요.

sentences.en: Looks like it's raining outside.
I think I misheard.

points.head: -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요  I think it will
points.tip: A guess about the future, or a softened "I'm going to".

sentences.en: I think it'll be cold tomorrow.
I think I'll be a little late. Sorry!

points.head: -잖아요  you know (we both know)
points.tip: Points to something the listener already knows.

sentences.en: I told you yesterday, remember?
It's the weekend, you know. Get some rest.

points.head: -(으)ㄹ까 봐  in case · afraid that
points.tip: You do the first thing because you're worried the second might happen.

sentences.en: I left early in case there was traffic.
I wrote it down in case I forgot.

lessons.title: Changing perspective — the piano upstairs (a short story)
lessons.note: On purpose, nothing is explained here. Learn the whole story by heart and the grammar sinks in by itself.

sentences.ko: 작년에 일 때문에 서울에서 살{게 됐어요|2}.
sentences.rd: jangnyeone il ttaemune seoureseo salge dwaesseoyo.
sentences.en: Last year, I {ended up|2} living in Seoul for work.

sentences.rd: je cheot wollumeun changmuneuro sani boyeosseoyo.
sentences.en: From the window of my first studio, {you could see|1} the mountains.

sentences.rd: geureonde bammada witjibeseo piano soriga deullyeosseoyo.
sentences.en: But every night, {I could hear|1} a piano upstairs.

sentences.ko: 처음엔 시끄러웠는데, 점점 그 소리가 좋{아졌어요|4}.
sentences.rd: cheoeumen sikkeureowonneunde, jeomjeom geu soriga joajyeosseoyo.
sentences.en: At first it was noisy, but little by little the sound {grew on|4} me.

sentences.ko: 어느 날 쓰레기를 버리러 나갔는데, 바람에 문이 {닫혀|1} {버렸어요|3}.
sentences.rd: eoneu nal sseuregireul beorireo naganneunde, barame muni datyeo beoryeosseoyo.
sentences.en: One day I stepped out to take out the trash, and the wind {slammed|1} the door shut {behind me|3}.

sentences.ko: 열쇠는 안에 있었어요. 문은 절대 안 {열렸어요|1}.
sentences.rd: yeolsoeneun ane isseosseoyo. muneun jeoldae an yeollyeosseoyo.
sentences.en: My keys were inside. The door just would not {open|1}.

sentences.ko: 그때 윗집 사람이 내려와서 저를 자기 집에서 기다리{게 했어요|5}.
sentences.rd: geuttae witjip sarami naeryeowaseo jeoreul jagi jibeseo gidarige haesseoyo.
sentences.en: Just then, the upstairs neighbor came down and {had me|5} wait at her place.

sentences.ko: 그분은 피아노 선생님이었어요. 열쇠 기사님을 기다리는 동안 피아노를 배우{게 됐어요|2}.
sentences.rd: geubuneun piano seonsaengnimieosseoyo. yeolsoe gisanimeul gidarineun dongan pianoreul baeuge dwaesseoyo.
sentences.en: She was a piano teacher. While we waited for the locksmith, I {ended up|2} learning the piano.

sentences.ko: 선생님은 저한테 매일 십 분씩 연습하{게 했어요|5}.
sentences.rd: seonsaengnimeun jeohante maeil sip bunssik yeonseupage haesseoyo.
sentences.en: She {made me|5} practice ten minutes a day.

sentences.ko: 손가락이 조금씩 빨{라졌어요|4}. 그래서 저도 작은 전자 피아노를 사 {버렸어요|3}.
sentences.rd: songaragi jogeumssik ppallajyeosseoyo. geuraeseo jeodo jageun jeonja pianoreul sa beoryeosseoyo.
sentences.en: My fingers {got|4} a little faster. So I {went ahead and|3} bought a small keyboard.

sentences.ko: 요즘은 아랫집에서 제 피아노 소리가 {들린대요|1}. 죄송해요, 아랫집!
sentences.rd: yojeumeun araetjibeseo je piano soriga deullindaeyo. joesonghaeyo, araetjip!
sentences.en: These days, the people downstairs say they {can hear|1} my piano. Sorry, downstairs!

footnotes: 보이다 · 들리다 · 열리다 · 닫히다 — the thing seen / heard / opened becomes the subject: 산이 보여요 (the mountain is visible) vs 산을 봐요 (I look at the mountain).
-게 되다 = "ended up / came to" — it happened, not exactly by your plan.
-아/어 버리다 = "…and that's that": the action is completely done, often with regret (닫혀 버렸어요) or a sense of relief / no going back (사 버렸어요).
-아/어지다 = becoming: 좋다 → 좋아지다 (come to like), 빠르다 → 빨라지다 (get faster). -게 하다 = make or let someone do something.

points.head: 보이다 · 들리다 · 열리다 · 닫히다  passive verbs
points.tip: The thing that is seen, heard or opened takes 이/가.

sentences.en: You can see the ocean from here.
Can you hear me?

points.head: -게 되다  end up / come to
points.tip: A change or result that came about, not a plain choice.

sentences.en: I ended up working in Korea.
We'll be working together starting next month.

points.head: -아/어 버리다  completely (oops / done)
points.tip: The action is finished for good — usually with regret, sometimes relief.

sentences.en: I ate the whole cake.
The bus just left without me.

points.head: -아/어지다  become / get
points.tip: Adjective → change over time.

sentences.en: It's gotten really cold.
Korean is getting easier and easier.

points.head: -게 하다  make / let someone
points.tip: The causer takes 이/가 (or 은/는), the person made to act takes 을/를 or 한테.

sentences.en: My mom made me go to bed early.
Let the kids play outside.
